From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. 11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status of Seller materials:** Other side's draft; reviewed against Buyer Playbook only. No Seller characterisation is accepted as fact.

**Headline:** The Seller's "fair and balanced package" is in substance a request that we adopt our own unauthorised fallbacks (20% cap, 18 months) as opening positions, collapse the Fundamental/Title regime into the general regime, and accept whole-data-room disclosure plus a blanket buyer-knowledge bar. Several items the Seller describes as "addressed" or "settled" are, on the Seller's own Disclosure Letter, unresolved (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses). **Recommend rejecting the package as a whole and responding with a mark-up on the terms below.**

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; hold at 25%.** 20% is our conditional fallback and no written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft has been given — we cannot concede it.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only ("deductible") recovery (cl 12.2).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar ("tipping") recovery once exceeded.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject on all three limbs.** Seller's numbers are 5x ours and the deductible structure strips an additional AUD 250,000 off every recovery scenario.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months post-Completion; plus a sweep that any limitation applies to *all* Claims unless expressly excluded (cl 12.3/13).
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months; limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims expressly listed.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; hold at 24 months and delete the "all Claims" sweep.** 18 months is an unauthorised fallback (no Amelia Frost approval), and the sweep is a hidden general-regime override of Title/Tax/IP/indemnity/covenant claims.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regime — 100% of price cap, minimum 6-year period, outside de minimis, basket and any knowledge qualifier.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject outright.** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap recovery on the shares we are paying AUD 24m for at AUD 4.8m with an 18-month fuse.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) — no fraud carve-out appears anywhere.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum extent enforceable; non-waivable.
- **Recommendation:** **Non-negotiable insertion.** No one on our side has authority to waive this, and a drafting that purports to limit fraud liability is both commercially unacceptable and likely unenforceable in any event — we should not be the party testing that.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" (Sch 7; DL [1.1]–[1.2]).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only — matter disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify its nature and scope; no deemed disclosure of data room, public registers or prudent-search matters.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject whole-data-room and public-register disclosure; require a fair-disclosure standard.** Note DL [1.4] is a blanket non-admission — fine as a non-admission, but it confirms the Seller is disclosing documents, not facts, which is exactly what a fair-disclosure standard is meant to prevent.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter of which Buyer *or its advisers* had knowledge, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete the blanket exclusion. If any knowledge qualifier survives, it must be actual knowledge of named *Seller* knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry (qualifying Seller warranties), and never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete cl 8.3.** Combined with SPA-N-006, "discoverable" constructive knowledge would convert the warranty package into a nullity.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Says consent is "addressed"; reasonable endeavours only; condition deemed satisfied on delivery of written consent (cl 3/6.3). **But DL [2] confirms no final written consent and no evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.**
- **Buyer wants:** Condition precedent requiring (i) effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) Bluefen consent under cl 11.2, and (ii) evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are met, both before Completion; Buyer sole discretion to waive.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours; require effective consent + evidence as a CP.** Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m) — a material customer consent cannot rest on a best-efforts covenant.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion" (cl 2/7). **DL [3] confirms not repaid, no discharge in data room.**
- **Buyer wants:** Current payout letter; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective releases of all security delivered at Completion. Any post-completion release only with irrevocable bank undertaking AND Amelia Frost approval.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject post-completion release; require payout + funds-flow repayment + releases at Completion.** Debt-free/cash-free pricing is meaningless if we complete with AUD 3.2m of secured debt still on the balance sheet and change-of-control triggered under DD-003 cl 8.1.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** DD-005 AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in funds flow. **DL [5] confirms they are absent from the funds flow and silent on payroll tax/super/on-costs.**
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs (super, payroll tax, leave accruals) as a specific funds-flow line item funded by Seller, or treated as Debt / price deduction; Seller warranty that no other transaction bonuses exist.
- **Recommendation:** **Require specific itemisation and Seller funding; do not accept a silent funds flow.** "A matter for the Seller" has no legal effect — post-Completion the Company (i.e., us) is the employer who owes them.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate" (cl 11.1). DL [4]: DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open (not bank-verified); no receipt or confirmatory assignment in data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Broadened indemnity covering failure of title to / claims over all Ironquay-developed materials, costs of securing assignment, and third-party IP claims — while preserving the cl 7.3 cure (pay and obtain assignment). Pre-Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment and executed confirmatory assignment, or price retention.
- **Recommendation:** **Broaden the indemnity and add a payment/assignment deliverable.** The AUD 180,000 figure is unverified in either direction, so the indemnity must cover the title gap, not just a single payment number.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** DD-006 is a "preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material (cl 4.6/Sch 6). DL [6]: ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps) sent to unintended external address; access, scope and notification duty all undetermined.
- **Buyer wants:** Covenant to preserve all logs and evidence; complete the investigation pre-Completion with Buyer visibility; update obligation through Completion; specific indemnity for notification, regulatory and remediation costs arising from the incident; no materiality characterisation either way in the SPA.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept "not material"; require preservation, investigation, updates and a specific indemnity.** We assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or quantum — which is exactly why the risk must sit with the Seller rather than be dismissed.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are "ordinary-course operating costs". DL [8]: silent on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course; DD-008 and DD-011 to be read together.
- **Buyer wants:** Factual confirmation of timing, termination rights and accrual status; treatment to be determined on the facts — no automatic Debt classification or price deduction, but equally no acceptance of the "ordinary course" label.
- **Recommendation:** **Assess; request supporting detail before agreeing treatment.** If any renewal is a committed pre-Completion liability for post-Completion benefit, it belongs in the working capital/Debt mechanics — but we should not pre-judge that.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Limitations apply to "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"; Tax/IP "settled under the general regime"; Title folded into general caps.
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations, specific indemnities and covenants each in their own regime with their own cap/period; general limitations expressly confined to general Warranty Claims.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the catch-all and insert an express carve-out list.** The "unless expressly stated otherwise" formulation is a hidden general-regime override and must be reversed to "limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims".

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title to 100% evidenced by the DD-012 share register. DL [10] concedes this is merely "the source relied on" and that Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence — ASIC company extract and historical shareholder search, executed transfers/consents for any prior share movements, PPSR search for encumbrances over the shares and Company assets, board/shareholder authorisations and director certificates for Harbourglass's capacity; Completion deliverables to match.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept DD-012 as proof of title; obtain independent verification before signing.** An internal register prepared by the Seller is a supplied source, not evidence, and the Seller's own letter says as much.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP positions "settled" under the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP remain OPEN as separate categories — separate caps and periods to be negotiated (tax period at least aligned to statutory amendment periods). We are not seeking unlimited liability and we accept no resolution has been reached.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject "settled"; record Tax and IP as open items.** Folding them into a 20%/18-month general regime is a substantive concession dressed as housekeeping, and nothing in our record shows agreement.

---

### Suggested cover note points for the response
1. The Seller's 20% cap and 18-month period are not accepted; Buyer's positions remain 25% / 24 months.
2. Fundamental/Title, Tax, IP, indemnities and covenants are separate regimes; delete the "all Claims" sweep and "all Claims of any nature" wording.
3. Fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out to be inserted across all limitation, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses.
4. Delete whole-data-room disclosure and cl 8.3 buyer-knowledge bar.
5. Bluefen (effective consent + evidence), Riverlark (payout, repayment, releases) and Ironquay (payment evidence + assignment) become Completion conditions/deliverables; DD-005 bonuses and on-costs become a funded funds-flow line.
6. DD-006 and Sandbar: further information requested; no materiality or treatment conceded.

**Internal note:** Two Seller asks (20% cap, 18 months) coincide with our internal fallbacks. If the team wishes to trade either at a later stage, written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the specific draft is required first — nothing in this review should be read as authorising those concessions.
